item.title: Towards New Parity Rules with Asynchronous Updating Inspired by Fat\`es's Rule
item.description: arXiv:2610.14026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The parity problem in 1D Cellular Automata is a classifier based on a local rule. If the number of ones in a ring of binary cells is odd then the automaton shall converge to all-one (11...11) else to all-zero (00...00). The objective is to find rules that are related to Fat\`es's Balanced Rule F but use less active neighborhoods (actions). The method is to analyze the effect of each actions and to find a functioning subset of the 12 actions used in rule F. New rules called HA, HB, HC, HF are defined with 10, 6, 4, 8 actions. Rule HC and HF need only three inputs whereas all others need four. The classification time of the rules was determined by averaging over many simulation runs with random initial configurations. It is almost the same for the rules HA and F, and is longer for the rules HB, HC, HF. In addition, the rule HD is defined, which updates three cells in parallel and works faster. In future work, the functioning and performance of the proposed rules should be treated in a more formal way, and related rules (also with different update schemes) could be considered.
item.dc:creator: Rolf Hoffmann

item.title: Geometry-Controlled Initial-Density Dependence in Branching-Merging Exclusion Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.15333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study geometry-controlled, initial-density-dependent stationary states in exclusion processes with branching-merging structures. We consider two boundary geometries for connecting the parallel branches to the reservoirs: the \(1\)-\(n\)-\(1\) model, in which a single lane branches into \(n\) parallel lanes and then merges back into a single lane, and the \(0\)-\(n\)-\(0\) model, in which particles directly enter and leave the \(n\) parallel lanes. For both models, we derive critical initial densities separating the low-density, shock-wave, and high-density regimes, and show that the theoretical predictions reproduce the phase diagrams and branch-averaged densities observed in simulations. In the \(1\)-\(n\)-\(1\) geometry, the critical initial densities depend on both the number of branches and the lengths of the upstream and downstream single-lane segments, whereas in the \(0\)-\(n\)-\(0\) geometry the corresponding estimates depend only on the number of branches. These results show that initial-condition dependence can arise from the global geometry of a branching-merging exclusion process, even without an explicit friction rule at the merging point.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Yamamoto, Daichi Yanagisawa, Katsuhiro Nishinari

item.title: When do lazy and invertible cellular automata generate all cellular automata?
item.description: arXiv:2610.18480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $A$ be a set with at least two elements. A lazy cellular automaton over $A^G$ acts as the identity except at the cells where a fixed pattern occurs, where it replaces the central symbol by a fixed different symbol. Let $M(G;A)$ be the submonoid of $\mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ generated by the lazy and the invertible cellular automata. We study when $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. Since no lazy cellular automaton is surjective, every surjective element of $M(G;A)$ is invertible; hence $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ whenever $A$ is infinite or $G$ has an element of infinite order. Moreover, if $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has a quotient isomorphic to the Klein four-group $C_2 \times C_2$, then $M(G;A) \neq \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$. For locally finite $G$, and in particular for finite $G$, these are the only obstructions: we prove that $M(G;A) = \mathrm{CA}(G;A)$ if and only if $3 \leq |A| < \infty$, or $|A| = 2$ and $G$ has no quotient isomorphic to $C_2 \times C_2$.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'a-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez

item.title: Frobenius Revivals in Laplacian Cellular Automata: Replication, Entropy, and Information Recovery
item.description: arXiv:2511.17389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate Frobenius revivals in prime-modulus Laplacian cellular automata. The Frobenius identity yields exact superpositions of translated, coefficient-weighted seed copies at prime-power times; we distinguish this algebraic replication from their geometric separation. We investigate seed recovery from separated replicas and evaluate the correction of independent symbol errors introduced during transmission of encoded configurations. For the diagonal neighborhood, we determine the exact periods of moving corner operators on square windows and establish sufficient conditions for recovering any binary seed under a binary--ternary--binary schedule. The results connect prime-power algebraic structure with spatial pattern formation and precisely delimited forms of information recovery.
item.dc:creator: Ma{\l}gorzata Nowak-K\k{e}pczyk

item.title: Idempotence criteria for lazy cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.11811v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A lazy cellular automaton $\tau:A^G\to A^G$ is determined by a finite neighborhood $S\subseteq G$ containing the group identity $e$, a pattern $p\in A^S$, and a writing symbol $a\in A\setminus\{p(e)\}$: its local rule is equal to the projection to $e$ except when it reads the pattern $p$, in which case it writes $a$. For a nonempty subset $T$ of the fiber $S_a:= p^{-1}(a)$, we introduce compatibility conditions on $p$ along the right translates $St$, $t\in T$. We show that, over every group, the existence of a compatible set is necessary for $\tau$ to be non-idempotent, and that it is also sufficient whenever $st = ts$ for all $t \in S_a$, $s \in S_{p(e)}$. In particular, compatibility characterizes non-idempotence over abelian groups, which reduces deciding idempotence to a search over subsets of $S_a$. Finally, for every dihedral group $D_n$ with $n\geq 4$, we construct an idempotent lazy cellular automaton that admits a compatible set, showing that the commutation hypothesis cannot simply be dropped.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Alcal\'{a}-Arroyo, Alonso Castillo-Ramirez, Maria G. Maga\~na-Ch\'avez, Luguis de los Santos Ba\~nos
